To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Co+ ion implantation can be used for the synthesis of Co quantum dots in SiO2 matrix, and that these dots exhibit electron field emission properties at room temperature.
Co+ ion-implantation into SiO2 matrix at room temperature leads to the formation of Co nanoclusters with a narrow size distribution.
the Co quantum dots in SiO2 layer have a staircase I-V curve and the Coulomb blockade effect can be controlled by changing the size and distribution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fabrication and characterization of Co quantum dots embedded in SiO2 layers by ion implantation.
the synthesis and characterisation of Co nanoparticles in SiO2 matrix by ion implantation.
the synthesis of Co nanoparticles by ion implantation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Co nanoparticles can be successfully implanted into the SiO2 layer and the size of these nanoclusters can be controlled by the implantation dose and energy.
the electron field emission properties of Co quantum dots embedded in SiO2 matrix can be tuned by controlling the size and the distribution of the nanocrystals.
Co+ ion implanted SiO2 matrix on silicon substrate is a very promising material for field emission applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully synthesised Co nanoclusters in SiO2 matrix by Co+ ion implantation and the size and distribution can be controlled by changing implantation dose and energy.
we have successfully synthesized Co nanoparticles by Co+ implantations and we have also demonstrated the Coulomb blockade in these quantum dots.
Co quantum dots in SiO2 matrix can be synthesised by Co ion implantation and the size and distribution are controllable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have successfully demonstrated that the quantum dot size can be controlled by varying the ion implantation conditions (energy, dose and annealing temperature).
the Co quantum dots embedded in the SiO2 layer can be a promising material for future nanoelectronic applications.
the Coulomb blockade can be observed at room temperature in Co quantum dots in SiO2 matrix synthesized by ion implantation.
